title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system
what_it_shows: A publicly traded holding company (SEC registrant) with three operating divisions, each a separate legal subsidiary: the Hospital System, the Health Plan and the College of Nursing and Health Sciences (acquired 2023). Corporate shared services (identity, data centers, network, cloud, security operations, ERP, HR, finance, legal and internal audit) sit in the parent. No affiliated covered entity designation (45 CFR 164.105(b)) is recorded for the Hospital System and the Health Plan. Organization charts show the Group CISO, Group Chief Risk Officer, Group Chief Privacy Officer, the three division security and compliance leads, and group internal audit reporting to the board audit committee

title: Group: HR roster by division
source_system: Group HR system (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees: Hospital System 29,000, Health Plan 8,000, College 2,000, corporate 6,000. College employees moved to group HR and payroll in 2024. Termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance for the Hospital System, Health Plan and corporate workforce

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger (SYS-G4); FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Revenue of about $18.0 billion: Hospital System about $10.5 billion, Health Plan about $7.1 billion in premiums and fees, College about $0.4 billion

title: Group: intercompany agreement register
source_system: Group legal contract management system
what_it_shows: Intercompany BAAs between the parent and each covered entity: Hospital System signed 2021, Health Plan signed 2022. The 2021 Hospital System BAA covers the Hospital System's own PHI and does not mention community-connect practices' PHI that corporate hosts; the 2022 Health Plan BAA covers the ASO plans' PHI. The 2025 College intercompany services agreement requires same-day phone notice to the College of an incident affecting its data, then written notice, and does not state the FERPA 99.33(a) redisclosure limits. A 2023 intercompany data sharing addendum covers the admission-notice (ADT) feed from the Hospital System to Health Plan care management, relying on 164.506(c)(4); no minimum-necessary protocol is attached to it

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication and sign-in policy export
source_system: Group identity platform admin console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: About 43,000 Hospital System, Health Plan and corporate workforce users sign in through SYS-G1 with MFA (push with number matching) for email and remote access; phishing-resistant authenticators for administrators only; lockout for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts; passwords of at least 14 characters checked against breached-password lists; remote sessions use TLS 1.2 or higher through the group VPN or zero-trust access service. The College's 2,000 staff are not on SYS-G1

title: Group: SYS-G1 identity governance export and policy
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows driven by HR events, with role requests approved by managers; identifiers issued from HR records and never reused; federated accounts disabled after 90 days of inactivity; agency and locum accounts expire at the end date entered by the staffing office; emergency accounts expire after 72 hours; account events forwarded to the SIEM. Student and trainee EHR accounts are not in identity governance

title: Group: Q1 2026 access certification results
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Quarterly certification completed for Hospital System and Health Plan applications and privileged roles; EHR managers certify their staff's access. Health Plan quarterly reviews were completed late twice in 2025

title: Group: privileged access management inventory, policy and session records
source_system: Privileged access management console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Administrators hold separate privileged accounts; elevation is just in time with approval and session recording for data center, cloud and application administrators; phishing-resistant MFA required. EHR, ancillary and claims vendors use named vendor accounts in PAM with approval per session and recording, with broad rights once connected. 103 of the 140 medical device vendor connections are brokered through PAM. Only the EHR release team can promote changes to production, through PAM

title: Group: directory forest and tier review
source_system: Group directory (DC1 and DC2); identity team review notes
what_it_shows: One directory forest serves DC1 and DC2 and every division except the College. EHR, ancillary, Health Plan claims core and group file service servers are joined to it. The highest-privilege tier is not isolated from other tiers. Sealed break-glass accounts exist for each critical system and are tested quarterly

title: Group: SIEM data sources, detection rules, retention and coverage map
source_system: Group SIEM (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC. Onboarded sources: SYS-G1 sign-ins and account events, EDR, firewalls, data center servers, cloud accounts, EHR application logs and privileged sessions. Not in the data source list: device networks at 4 hospitals (no network detection sensors), the 37 device vendor connections outside PAM, College campus networks, the College directory and College SaaS logs. Rules for failed sign-ins and sign-in anomalies; correlation of identity, EDR, firewall and EHR logs; review workflows in the case system; storage is write-once and administered by the SOC platform team; logs kept 1 year online and 6 years archived. Network detection at the data center edge includes an outbound volume rule; no rule per share group

title: Group: SOC case export, playbooks and exercise log, April 2025 to March 2026
source_system: Group case management system (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Incidents tracked in one case system with group playbooks, severity ratings and discovery dates recorded for each covered entity; a Hospital System liaison joins every Severity 1 or 2 bridge and a Health Plan liaison joins Health Plan cases; SOC triage metrics reported monthly. Technical playbooks exercised each quarter; no exercise covered cross-division notification or ransomware downtime and diversion. SOC analysts and division liaisons trained in 2025. College incidents are recorded in College IT records, not in the group case system

title: Group: incident response plan v5 (2025) and draft notification matrix
source_system: Group SOC document library; Group legal
what_it_shows: Group IR plan v5 (2025) with structure, roles, reportable incidents and metrics; it does not cover the College or link to the hospitals' emergency plan incident command and diversion steps. A draft multi-regulator notification matrix started in 2026 lists both covered entities, state attorneys general and the SEC; state insurance commissioner contacts, Federal Student Aid and FTC Safeguards Rule contacts and clocks are not entered; it has not been exercised

title: Group: disclosure committee charter and FY2025 Form 10-K Item 106 disclosure
source_system: SEC filings; corporate secretary
what_it_shows: The charter covers cybersecurity incidents and sets Form 8-K Item 1.05 review steps. The Item 106 disclosure describes board risk committee oversight and the Group CISO's reporting line. No cross-division exercise of the disclosure process is recorded

title: Group: EDR coverage report
source_system: EDR console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: EDR on all servers and workstations in the Hospital System, the Health Plan and corporate, including downtime workstations, servers in DC1 and DC2 and cloud workloads; on College servers since 2025. Medical devices are not listed (no agent support)

title: Group: vulnerability scan and configuration compliance reports, Q1 2026
source_system: Vulnerability scanner; configuration management console
what_it_shows: Weekly authenticated scans of data center servers, including HCIS servers, and cloud hosts; critical findings on group-managed servers fixed within 15 days; server and workstation hardening checked weekly. Device networks at 4 hospitals are excluded from scanning, with no passive discovery

title: Group: external penetration test report, 2026-03
source_system: Third-party testing firm report
what_it_shows: Annual external penetration test of the data centers and the EHR web services, completed in 2026-03

title: Group: data center network design, firewall rule review and zone diagram
source_system: Firewall management; network documentation (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Next-generation firewalls deny by default at external boundaries, with rule base reviews on file. EHR web, application and database tiers sit in separate zones. Inside each data center, HCIS, Health Plan claims core and College file share server zones are not separated from each other. Encrypted private links from DC1 and DC2 to providers A and B. Each hospital has diverse WAN carriers; EDs and command centers have analog lines and EMS radios

title: Group: data center facility, access, media and capacity records (DC1 and DC2)
source_system: Data center badge system; facilities records; colocation operator reports
what_it_shows: Badge and biometric entry with escorts and cameras; access lists approved by the infrastructure director and reviewed each quarter; data center media sanitized or destroyed with certificates. DC2 is a colocation facility about 300 miles from DC1 whose operator controls the building perimeter, with capacity for the full EHR and ancillary systems. Capacity monitoring reports for the EHR tiers in both data centers

title: Group: cloud account inventory, IAM and guardrail report, providers A and B
source_system: Cloud provider consoles; guardrail policy service (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Provider A landing zone holds the Health Plan UM platform, member and broker portals and the HCIS imaging archive tier in their own accounts; provider B holds the immutable backup vault. Cloud roles are federated from SYS-G1 with no long-lived keys for people. Hub firewalls deny by default between division accounts and to the internet; the archive tier is reachable only from PACS over the private link. Guardrails enforce encryption, no public storage and approved regions; 2% of resources had deviations without an approved exception. The central log archive is write-once, administered only by the SOC platform team, with 1 year searchable and 6 years archived

title: Group: encryption settings and key management inventory
source_system: Key management services; database, storage and endpoint consoles (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: EHR and ancillary databases and storage, the group file service, the imaging archive tier, the member portal database and the vault are encrypted at rest with group-managed keys rotated each year; downtime and clinical workstations use full-disk encryption; validated cryptographic module certificates on file

title: Group: backup policy, vault immutability settings and restore test log
source_system: Backup service and immutable vault (provider B)
what_it_shows: Daily immutable copies of data center and cloud workloads kept 35 days in a separate provider and account under a separate backup identity that group directory credentials cannot reach; EHR storage snapshots every 15 minutes in DC1 and DC2; automatic integrity checks; monthly sample file restores recorded. The restore log lists no restore of the full EHR from the vault

title: Group: external and partner TLS configuration scan, Q1 2026
source_system: Group SOC scanning tool
what_it_shows: WAN, partner and remote access endpoints accept TLS 1.2 or higher only

title: Group: policy and standards library
source_system: Group policy repository (intranet)
what_it_shows: Group policies POL-01 to POL-05 (pre-2026 versions) aligned to CSF 2.0 and published on the intranet, with printed copies in hospital downtime binders. Group standards for logging, configuration management, identification and authentication, continuity, cryptography and assessment procedures. Hospital System and Health Plan supplements to the current group policies; no College supplement; the College adopted the group policies in 2024 and its 2022 IT standards remain in use. The policy register keeps documents 6 years

title: Group: common control catalog and inheritance matrices
source_system: Group GRC tool
what_it_shows: 99 common and hybrid controls, each with a named provider. Inheritance documented for the Hospital System (2024 matrix) and the Health Plan (2025 matrix). For the College the catalog marks controls as inherited, partly inherited or not inherited because it runs its own directory

title: Group: risk management strategy, monitoring reports and board risk committee minutes, 2025 to Q1 2026
source_system: Group GRC tool; corporate secretary
what_it_shows: Risk acceptance by level: Low by the division security and compliance lead, Moderate by the division president, High by the Group Chief Risk Officer with the Group CISO, Very High by the board risk committee only; patient-safety risks rated High must be treated. Continuous monitoring strategy and quarterly control metrics to the Hospital System risk committee. Quarterly cyber risk reports to the board risk committee; the minutes record no written report on the College's information security program

title: Group: internal audit charter and 2026 audit plan
source_system: Group internal audit
what_it_shows: Internal audit reports to the board audit committee and neither designs nor operates controls. The 2026 plan schedules the common control assessment with division samples for July and August and adds the College for the first time

title: Group: training, phishing exercise and acknowledgment records
source_system: Learning management system; phishing simulation platform
what_it_shows: Employee security and privacy training completion of 98%; monthly phishing exercises and monthly reminders on the awareness calendar; annual module includes insider threat and privacy snooping cases; annual POL-05 acknowledgments; EHR training before account activation; SOC and incident command staff training records. For students and trainees the hospitals hold the schools' training attestations and no completion records

title: Group: HR procedures, screening and termination records
source_system: Group HR system (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: Background checks before hire and licensure verification for clinical staff; onboarding checklist includes security responsibilities; HR termination events disable SYS-G1 accounts, immediately for involuntary terminations; staffing agency and locum contracts require end dates

title: Group: sanctions procedure and sanctions logs, 2025 to Q1 2026
source_system: Group HR and division privacy offices
what_it_shows: Sanctions applied and documented by HR with each division's Privacy Officer; logs for 2025 and Q1 2026 by division

title: Group: vendor master, third-party risk register and contract templates
source_system: ERP vendor master (SYS-G4); third-party risk management tool
what_it_shows: Tiered vendor program with a supply chain risk management plan covering clinical software and device vendors; tier 1 clinical vendors (EHR, laboratory, imaging, pharmacy automation) reviewed each year by SOC 2 report or questionnaire. Contract templates include BAAs, security requirements, vulnerability notification and support-life commitments; they do not require signed updates or software bills of materials. College vendors are reviewed by College staff and are not in the program. The vendor master is the source of the intake vendor register

title: Group: vendor SOC 2 reports on file
source_system: Vendor portals (cloud providers A and B, DC2 colocation operator, EHR vendor, telehealth vendor)
what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports for cloud providers A and B and the DC2 colocation operator (physical security), the EHR vendor (its support and release environment, not the group-hosted instance) and the telehealth vendor, each reviewed within the past 12 months

title: Group: AI tool discovery
source_system: Procurement records; SaaS discovery and SYS-G1 app list; EHR module configuration; model registries
what_it_shows: AI in use or planned: the EHR vendor's sepsis prediction model at 9 hospitals since 2025, an inpatient deterioration index, a CT intracranial hemorrhage triage tool at the flagship, an ED AI scribe pilot (60 physicians), a proposed portal reply drafting feature, the Health Plan's prior authorization triage model in shadow mode and its fraud, waste and abuse model, the College's online proctoring and AI tutoring assistant, and an enterprise generative AI assistant piloted with about 3,000 users under a BAA. A Group AI council charter and a Group AI Standard are dated 2026

title: Group: records retention schedule
source_system: Group records management
what_it_shows: Security records kept 6 years; medical records kept per the law of each state where the hospitals operate

what_it_shows: The Group CISO leads the program. The Hospital System security and compliance lead is designated the hospital covered entity's Security Official and the Health Plan lead the Health Plan's Security Official; each covered entity designates its own Privacy Officer. The Hospital System Section 1557 Coordinator (45 CFR 92.7) is named

title: Group: email and collaboration service policy export
source_system: Collaboration and email SaaS admin console
what_it_shows: Vendor spam and malware filtering; the group sets sender authentication, attachment rules and external-email banners. Staff mass notification for the hospitals uses group email and SMS through SYS-G1

title: Group: group file service share permission report
source_system: Group file service (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Shares for the Hospital System, the Health Plan and (since 2025) the College's registrar, financial aid and HR offices in DC1; permissions set per division and reviewed each quarter. College shares were migrated with their old permission groups, and registrar and financial aid shares are open to broad College staff groups. Health Plan reporting shares hold member data extracts with no purge schedule

title: Hospital System: licensure, certification and service line report
source_system: Hospital System licensure and CMS certification files
what_it_shows: 9 acute-care hospitals with 3,620 licensed beds (a 960-bed flagship with a Level I trauma center and 8 community hospitals of 140 to 420 beds; all have 100 or more beds), 6 in Florida and 3 in two neighboring states; 9 EDs with about 610,000 visits a year; about 186,000 admissions a year and about 3,000 inpatients a day; 46 outpatient sites. Every hospital participates in Medicare and Medicaid. No transplant program; no hospital holds itself out as providing substance use disorder diagnosis, treatment or referral as a specialized program

title: Hospital System: patient volume and shared patient report
source_system: EHR reporting (SYS-H1)
what_it_shows: About 3.4 million patients with an encounter in the last 3 years, in 3 states; about 140,000 Health Plan members were hospital patients in the last 12 months. Patient counts by state are produced by a manual query

title: Hospital System: revenue cycle and payer enrollment records
source_system: Revenue cycle reporting (SYS-H1); payer enrollment files
what_it_shows: Medicare and Medicaid enrollment for all 9 hospitals; claims and eligibility sent as standard electronic transactions through a clearinghouse

title: Hospital System: HCIS component inventory, baselines and architecture documents
source_system: Configuration management database; HCIS architecture repository
owner: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
what_it_shows: EHR web, application and database tiers in DC1 with a replicated copy in DC2; about 640 downtime workstations; an active-passive clinical interface engine across DC1 and DC2; laboratory and blood bank systems; PACS and vendor-neutral archive with an archive tier at provider A; pharmacy automation servers; baselines for EHR servers, database servers, clinical and downtime workstations. The unsupported component register lists 11 ancillary servers (analyzer middleware and two pharmacy automation servers) on an unsupported operating system in restricted zones. Devices and analyzers that feed the interface engine are not linked to their interfaces in the inventory

title: Hospital System: EHR user, role and security class report
source_system: EHR admin console (SYS-H1)
owner: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
what_it_shows: About 34,000 workforce user accounts, each unique; about 1,900 security templates mapped to job codes; cross-site access limited to transfer center, health information management and system pharmacist roles; sensitive-record flags for behavioral health, Part 2 records received from outside programs and employee-as-patient; only the EHR security team can change security classes, with team lead approval; EHR sessions end after 30 minutes on shared and 60 minutes on assigned workstations. Students and trainees (about 4,500 a year) hold local EHR accounts

title: Hospital System: student and trainee account records and roster files
source_system: EHR security team request queue; roster emails from schools
owner: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
what_it_shows: About 4,500 students and trainees a year rotate through the hospitals (about 3,100 from the College and about 1,400 from 22 outside schools). The EHR security team creates their local EHR accounts from rosters emailed by the schools as spreadsheets; accounts have no end date and sign in with a password only. The hospitals hold the schools' clearance and training attestations

title: Hospital System: school affiliation agreements
source_system: Hospital System contract files
what_it_shows: Affiliation agreements with the College and 22 outside schools. The agreements do not require schools to report withdrawals or schedule changes, and do not define clearance or notice duties; the hospitals rely on the schools' training attestations

title: Hospital System: EHR audit, privacy monitoring and break-glass records
source_system: EHR admin console and privacy monitoring tool (SYS-H1)
what_it_shows: Audit generation on for all EHR modules and the ancillary systems: record views, prints, exports, orders, results, security point changes and break-glass use, with user, patient, workstation, time, action and department; events forwarded to the SIEM; EHR access logs kept 7 years. Privacy monitoring rules (VIP, coworker, family, same surname) across 9 hospitals; alerts reviewed weekly, VIP and employee-as-patient alerts investigated within 5 business days; break-glass use reviewed by the Privacy Officer; case log on file

title: Hospital System: EHR change control, release and integrity records
source_system: EHR change management system; build repository; file integrity monitoring console
owner: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
what_it_shows: The EHR change control board approves build, upgrade and interface changes, with emergency changes reviewed the next business day; each change carries a clinical safety and security impact review; build analysts cannot promote their own changes and only the release team promotes to production; local build is version-controlled; pharmacy formulary and drug library changes are logged and need a second pharmacist; file integrity monitoring on EHR application servers. Vendor updates are tested for function in staging; package integrity is not verified

title: Hospital System: HCIS contingency plan v4 (2025) and recovery runbooks
source_system: HCIS document library
owner: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
what_it_shows: Plan v4 (2025) covers site loss with failover to DC2 and clinical downtime procedures, with recovery objectives (8-hour RTO for the EHR), priorities, roles and contacts; it assumes DC2 is clean and does not refer to the emergency plan's diversion and transfer steps. Recovery runbooks restore to DC2. The infrastructure team's estimate for rebuilding the EHR from the vault is 5 to 7 days; no test supports it. A design document (draft) describes a clean recovery environment at provider B planned for 2027-03-31

title: Hospital System: DC2 failover test report, 2026-04
source_system: Infrastructure test records
what_it_shows: The annual failover test brought the EHR back at DC2 in 1 hour 40 minutes. The report records that DC2 relies on the same directory forest as DC1

title: Hospital System: downtime workstation inventory, test logs and super user roster
source_system: HCIS downtime program records
owner: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
what_it_shows: About 640 downtime workstations on every nursing unit and in every ED, with full-disk encryption, local printers, application allow-listing and a 5-minute lock; census, medication and results reports refresh every 2 hours. Test logs show quarterly tests, except at 3 community hospitals with no test in the last 12 months. Downtime super users on every unit complete an annual module; ED and pharmacy staff drill paper workflows each year. Paper procedures and back-entry steps are written for outages of hours

title: Hospital System: clinical workstation configuration baseline
source_system: Endpoint management console
what_it_shows: Clinical workstations lock after 10 minutes idle (2 minutes in public areas) and unlock with badge tap and PIN; the badge locks after 5 failed PIN attempts; full-disk encryption on all workstations

title: Hospital System: ancillary server patch and support status report
source_system: Patch management console
owner: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
what_it_shows: Operating system patches applied monthly; ancillary clinical servers wait for vendor validation, and the median time to apply critical patches on them is 47 days against the 30-day target; 11 ancillary servers run an unsupported operating system

title: Hospital System: interface route inventory, interface agreement register and ADT feed specification
source_system: Clinical interface engine (SYS-H2); interface agreement register
owner: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
what_it_shows: Routes to the laboratory, imaging, pharmacy automation, the health information exchange, state and county public health agencies, the clearinghouse and the Health Plan; interface agreements for the reference laboratory, the health information exchange and public health; HL7 interfaces over VPN or TLS with acknowledgments and integrity checks. The admission-notice feed to Health Plan care management is limited to shared members and sends full ADT segments

title: Hospital System: interface and service account register
source_system: Interface engine and ancillary system account register
owner: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
what_it_shows: 63 interface and service accounts used by the interface engine and ancillary systems have static passwords older than 1 year

title: Hospital System: privacy office records
source_system: Hospital System privacy office
what_it_shows: The Notice of Privacy Practices; a disclosure inventory documenting purposes for treatment, payment and operations uses, with no minimum-necessary protocol for routine disclosures to the Health Plan; Part 2 records received from outside programs are flagged in the EHR and handled by the Privacy Officer case by case

title: Hospital System: medical device and clinical OT inventory
source_system: Clinical engineering management system
what_it_shows: About 52,000 networked medical devices plus nurse call, building automation and medical gas alarm systems. The inventory is about 81% complete, and devices that store ePHI are not all tracked to a location and owner. About 6,900 devices (13%) run unsupported operating systems. Device security review at purchase; infusion pump drug libraries held by clinical engineering

title: Hospital System: device network zone reports for 9 hospitals
source_system: Network management system
what_it_shows: Device network segmentation is complete at 5 of 9 hospitals; at the other 4, device, OT and user networks share flat segments. The drug library server is on a segmented network at the 5 segmented hospitals only

title: Hospital System: device vendor remote connection inventory
source_system: Clinical engineering records; PAM console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: 140 device vendor remote support connections: 103 through group PAM; 37 bypass PAM, use shared vendor credentials and stay connected

title: Hospital System: unified emergency preparedness program documents
source_system: System emergency management library
what_it_shows: All 9 hospitals elected a unified and integrated program (board resolution and program charter); each hospital's emergency manager sits on the system committee. The plan was reviewed 2025-06, with policies and the communication plan reviewed in 2025. Hazard vulnerability analyses for each hospital and the community (2025) score an IT outage as a single-site event; none covers simultaneous EHR downtime at all 9 hospitals. Strategies cover hurricanes, surge, utility loss and mass casualties, with no system-level diversion criteria for an IT outage. Continuity of operations plans list service capabilities and succession and assume the EHR or DC2 is available. Facility access procedures; hospital annexes for trauma, burn and pediatric services; membership in regional health care coalitions; transfer agreements point mostly to other group hospitals; paper transfer packets; analog lines and radios in EDs and command centers; staff mass notification through group email and SMS

title: Hospital System: emergency exercise records, after-action reports and training, 2024 to Q1 2026
source_system: System emergency management library
what_it_shows: Two exercises per hospital per year on the exercise calendar, including the regional coalition full-scale exercise; the 2025 additional exercise was a mass-casualty drill; the plan was activated for a 2024 hurricane; after-action reports filed for each; regional status system and radio reporting used in exercises. Emergency preparedness training at onboarding and every 2 years, with no multi-day IT downtime content

title: Hospital System: facility security, maintenance, generator and media records
source_system: Hospital security and facilities systems; destruction vendor certificates
what_it_shows: Badge access to hospital server and network closets managed by hospital security; facility security plans for each hospital; visitor validation; maintenance logs; generators tested per NFPA 110 with fuel plans and monitored over the network; certificates from a certified destruction vendor; drive wipe logs before reuse; equipment moves open a change record with a backup step

source_system: Flagship and 2 community hospitals (observation)
owner: Hospital System security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: Badge-tap workstations in clinical areas; privacy screens in public areas; downtime workstations locked, with printed downtime binders on the units

title: Hospital System: BAA register and BAA template review
source_system: Group legal contract management system
what_it_shows: BAAs with corporate (intercompany), the EHR vendor and the clinical vendors with PHI access, including ancillary system vendors, the reference laboratory, the health information exchange, the clearinghouse, the telehealth vendor, the AI scribe vendor (no-training terms) and the imaging AI vendor; written on the group template, which includes the 164.314(a)(2)(i) terms; no arrangements with governmental entities

title: Hospital System: community-connect agreements, federation records and practice attestations

Practices federate their own identity providers with MFA required by contract, attested by each practice and not technically verified; practices attest to their user lists and request users through federation, and the Hospital System approves the security templates. title: College: campus IT asset list, scan reports and change log

Semiannual vulnerability scans of campus networks; last penetration test 2023; change log for campus IT and SaaS configuration

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G1): account management
source_system: Identity governance configuration; joiner-mover-leaver sample (60 events across 3 divisions); EHR student account extract (July 2026); group identity director interview
what_it_shows: The 60 sampled joiner-mover-leaver events were processed through identity governance with approvals. Student and trainee EHR accounts (about 4,500 a year) are created from emailed rosters without an approval workflow, have no end date and are not in quarterly certification; schools are not required to report early departures. The July 2026 extract compared with school rotation calendars showed 412 student accounts active after their rotations ended

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G1): disable accounts
source_system: Inactivity and expiry job configuration; EHR student account extract
what_it_shows: The inactivity job disables federated accounts after 90 days and on termination; local student EHR accounts have no expiry date and are outside the job

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G1): privileged accounts
source_system: PAM policy; 25 privileged sessions
what_it_shows: The 25 sampled privileged sessions were elevated just in time through PAM with approval and recording

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G1): organizational user authentication
source_system: EHR and SYS-G1 user extracts; duplicate identity check
what_it_shows: Each user maps to one unique identity; the duplicate check found none

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G1): MFA for privileged accounts
source_system: PAM authentication policy; hardware-key sign-in test
what_it_shows: Administrator sign-in required the hardware key

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G1): authenticator management
source_system: Service account register; interface engine configuration files; password policy
what_it_shows: The password policy matches the group standard. 63 interface and service accounts have static passwords older than 1 year. Passwords for 9 interface accounts are stored in plain text in interface engine configuration files; reported to the Group CISO the same day

title: Control assessment: Common control (Group HR with SYS-G1): personnel termination
source_system: 25 terminations across 3 divisions; HR event to disable timestamps
what_it_shows: All 25 sampled terminations had SYS-G1 access disabled within 4 hours of the HR event, credentials revoked and exit steps recorded

title: Control assessment: Common control (Group HR): literacy training
source_system: Training completion reports; phishing exercise results; school affiliation agreements
what_it_shows: Employee training completion, monthly phishing exercise results and content updates are on file. The hospitals hold no record of security or privacy training for students and trainees before account activation, only the schools' attestations

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G2): system monitoring
source_system: SIEM data source list; network detection sensor map; vendor connection inventory
what_it_shows: Monitoring covers data centers, cloud accounts, identity and endpoints. The 37 device vendor connections outside PAM are not visible to the SOC; device networks at 4 hospitals and College campus networks have no network detection sensors; College SaaS logs are not collected

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G2): incident response testing
source_system: Exercise log 2025-2026
what_it_shows: The exercise log lists quarterly technical playbook tests; none tested the notification matrix, cross-division coordination, or ransomware downtime and diversion

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G2): incident handling
source_system: Incident tickets (20 sampled); playbooks; College incident records
what_it_shows: The 20 sampled tickets were handled under group playbooks through containment, eradication and recovery with lessons learned recorded. Incident handling is not linked to the hospitals' emergency plan, incident command or diversion decisions. College incidents are handled under its 2022 plan with its own severity scale and escalation

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G2): incident reporting
source_system: POL-03 (draft v2026); notification matrix draft
what_it_shows: POL-03 v2026 and the notification matrix were reviewed as drafts. Staff reporting to the SOC is defined; the matrix has no state insurance commissioner, Federal Student Aid or FTC Safeguards Rule contacts and clocks

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G2): incident response plan
source_system: Group IR plan v5; College IR plan (2022); distribution list
what_it_shows: Group IR plan v5 (2025) sets structure, roles, reportable incidents, metrics and approval. It does not address hospital downtime, diversion or the College's notice duties; information sharing with regulators is incomplete for the College and the Health Plan; it was not updated after the College acquisition or the 2025 file share move; it was not distributed to College IT or the financial aid office

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G2): vulnerability monitoring
source_system: Scan schedules and reports; device network scan exclusions
what_it_shows: Scan schedules, reports and remediation records match the standard for data center and cloud hosts; device networks at 4 hospitals are excluded from scanning with no passive discovery

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G3): system backup
source_system: Vault configuration; backup job reports; restore of 3 file sets
what_it_shows: Vault configuration and backup jobs match the standard; 3 file sets were restored from the vault

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G3): boundary protection
source_system: Firewall rule review; data center zone diagram; east-west traffic test
what_it_shows: External interfaces are monitored and controlled with deny-by-default rules. The east-west test, run with change approval, reached Health Plan claims servers from an HCIS application server; HCIS, claims and College file share zones can reach each other inside each data center

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G3): transmission protection
source_system: TLS scan of 80 endpoints
what_it_shows: All 80 scanned endpoints accepted TLS 1.2 or higher only

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G3): protection at rest
source_system: Encryption settings for EHR database, file service, and vault
what_it_shows: Encryption at rest is enabled for the EHR database, the file service and the vault

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G3): configuration settings
source_system: Guardrail compliance report; server hardening scan
what_it_shows: Hardening settings are documented, enforced and monitored; 2% of cloud resources have deviations without an approved exception

title: Control assessment: HCIS: access enforcement
source_system: EHR security class matrix; test of 6 roles across 3 hospitals
what_it_shows: Access under the 6 tested roles at 3 hospitals matched the security class matrix

title: Control assessment: HCIS: audit record review
source_system: Privacy monitoring case log; SOC case metrics
what_it_shows: Privacy monitoring alerts were reviewed weekly with cases logged and reported; SOC case metrics show review around the clock

title: Control assessment: HCIS: contingency plan
source_system: HCIS contingency plan v4; unified emergency plan; downtime procedures
what_it_shows: Plan v4 sets recovery objectives, priorities, roles and contacts for a site loss. It has no strategy for keeping clinical functions going if ransomware reaches both data centers and no plan for restoration into a clean environment; it is not coordinated with the IR plan or the emergency plan's incident command and diversion steps; the directory dependency found in the 2026 failover test has not been added

title: Control assessment: HCIS: contingency plan testing
source_system: Failover test report 2026-04; downtime workstation test logs (9 hospitals)
what_it_shows: The 2026-04 failover test results were reviewed with corrective actions; downtime workstations at 3 community hospitals were not tested in the last 12 months; no restore of the EHR from the vault has been run

title: Control assessment: HCIS: system recovery and reconstitution
source_system: Recovery runbooks; vault restore records
what_it_shows: Recovery within the 8-hour RTO is shown only for failover to DC2; no clean environment or tested sequence exists for reconstitution after a compromise of both data centers, where the estimate is 5 to 7 days

title: Control assessment: HCIS: flaw remediation
source_system: Patch compliance reports for ancillary servers; vendor validation records
what_it_shows: Flaws are identified, reported and corrected with vendor validation of updates. Median 47 days to apply critical software updates on ancillary servers against a 30-day target; firmware updates for 2 storage arrays and 4 analyzer gateways are more than 90 days late

title: Control assessment: HCIS: system component inventory
source_system: Configuration management database extract; interface route inventory
what_it_shows: The inventory lists HCIS servers, databases, interfaces and workstations without duplicates and is reviewed on schedule; devices and analyzers that send data through the interface engine are not in it, and their interface and owner are not recorded

title: Control assessment: Hospital System sample: nonlocal maintenance
source_system: Vendor connection inventory (140 connections); PAM vendor sessions; 3 hospitals' clinical engineering interviews
what_it_shows: All 140 device vendor connections reviewed: 103 run through PAM with approval per session and recording; 37 are not approved per session, are not monitored or recorded, use shared vendor credentials without MFA, and keep sessions and network connections open after maintenance

title: Control assessment: Hospital System sample: external personnel security

title: Control assessment: Hospital System sample: device network boundaries

title: Control assessment: Health Plan sample: external system services
